candidates.rule: Do not use `caplog` in provider tests; use direct log capture or logical assertions instead
candidates.trigger: caplog` appears in a test function in providers/**/*.py

candidates.rule: Avoid real `asyncio.sleep` calls in trigger unit tests; patch `asyncio.sleep` or use `asyncio.wait_for` to assert non-completion
candidates.trigger: asyncio.sleep` with a literal float/int appears inside a test function in providers/**/triggers/test_*.py

candidates.rule: When a parameter appends to rather than replaces spec-file content, docs, docstrings, test names, and example names must say 'appended'/'merged', not 'overrides'
candidates.trigger: A docstring or RST file uses the word 'overrides' for a parameter that the underlying library (pydantic-ai, etc.) merges/appends with the spec-file value

candidates.rule: When an operator parameter replaces a built-in default prompt rather than appending to it, the docstring must say 'overrides' not 'appended to'
candidates.trigger: An operator docstring says a `system_prompt` or similar param is 'appended to' or 'additional instructions' but the implementation assigns it directly (replacing the default)

candidates.rule: Plugin FastAPI sub-apps mounted under the Airflow webserver must add per-route or router-level `Depends(requires_access_*)` auth dependencies; do not rely on parent-app middleware alone
candidates.trigger: A FastAPI app or router is defined in `providers/**/plugins/*.py` and its route handlers lack `Depends(requires_access_*)` or equivalent auth dependency

candidates.rule: When adding a new operator entry to the operators `index.rst` table, also bump the operator count stated in the prose above the table and add a matching descriptive paragraph
candidates.trigger: A new `* -` row is added to the operators comparison table in `providers/**/docs/operators/index.rst` without updating the operator count sentence

candidates.rule: In `AIRFLOW_CONN_*` quickstart doc examples, encode `extra` as a nested JSON object, not as a JSON-serialised string
candidates.trigger: `extra` value in an `AIRFLOW_CONN_` shell export is a quoted JSON string (e.g. `'\"model\": ...'`) rather than a plain nested object

candidates.rule: Keep `provider.yaml` field descriptions consistent with the current schema; remove references to parameters that have been deleted
candidates.trigger: A `description:` value in `provider.yaml` references a field name that no longer exists in the same connection type block

candidates.rule: Example DAGs must be self-contained and copy-pasteable; do not extract shared helpers across example DAG files
candidates.trigger: A function or class defined outside an example DAG file is imported and used inside `providers/**/example_dags/*.py`

candidates.rule: Example DAGs must not wrap optional-dependency imports in `try/except`; import errors should surface immediately
candidates.trigger: A `try: import ...; except ImportError` block appears inside `providers/**/example_dags/*.py`

candidates.rule: Do not manually edit `get_provider_info.py`; all changes must go to `provider.yaml` and be regenerated via `prek run update-providers-build-files`
candidates.trigger: A diff modifies `providers/**/get_provider_info.py` directly without a corresponding change to the same provider's `provider.yaml`

candidates.rule: When a hook subclass ignores parent-signature parameters (e.g. `api_key`, `base_url`) in favour of `extra`, document this explicitly in the docstring
candidates.trigger: A method in `providers/**/hooks/*.py` has parameters with the same names as `extra` keys but reads from `extra` rather than the parameters without a docstring note

candidates.rule: When hook/operator docs claim a parameter overrides a spec-file value, the implementation must only pass that parameter conditionally (omit it when unset) so the spec file's value is used as a fallback
candidates.trigger: A hook method unconditionally passes a keyword argument to an underlying factory (e.g. `Agent.from_file(model=self.get_conn(), ...)`) when docs state the spec file supplies the default

candidates.rule: HITL XCom action fields that drive a poll loop must use Literal or Enum types, not bare str, to prevent infinite loops from typos
candidates.trigger: A dataclass or TypedDict field typed as `str` is used as a discriminator in a poll loop that checks for specific string values (e.g. "approve", "reject")

candidates.rule: Each provider hook subclass must declare its own `default_conn_name` that matches its specific `conn_type`, not inherit a generic parent's connection name
candidates.trigger: A hook subclass (e.g. `PydanticAIAzureHook`) does not override `default_conn_name` and inherits the parent's generic value

candidates.rule: Deferred operator `get_job_status` implementations must handle expired or deleted remote jobs by returning a non-active/non-succeeded status that causes the mixin to resubmit, not raise
candidates.trigger: A `get_job_status` method in a deferred operator does not catch the not-found/404 error from the remote API and instead lets it propagate as a hard task failure

candidates.rule: In Databricks trigger constructors, pass `owner=caller` to validation helpers rather than `owner=self.__class__.__name__` to stay consistent with the existing `caller` attribution pattern
candidates.trigger: A validation helper call inside a trigger `__init__` uses `owner=self.__class__.__name__` when the constructor already accepts a `caller: str` parameter

candidates.rule: Provider `changelog.rst` entries must be concise; do not include methodology notes, PR descriptions, or "add tests for…" clauses inline in the changelog line
candidates.trigger: A changelog entry in `docs/changelog.rst` contains parenthetical descriptions of test coverage, refactor rationale, or methodology (e.g. "Add tests for best-effort cancellation semantics…")

candidates.rule: Async provider hooks that call sync connection helpers must centralise version-gating logic in the `common` provider rather than duplicating version checks across individual provider hooks
candidates.trigger: An async hook in an individual provider directly wraps a sync connection call with an inline version check instead of delegating to a helper in `providers/common`

candidates.rule: In provider code, `Connection` must be imported from `airflow.models.connection`, not from `airflow.providers.common.compat.version_compat` or similar compat modules
candidates.trigger: A provider file imports `Connection` from a path other than `airflow.models.connection` (e.g. from `airflow.providers.common.compat.version_compat`)

candidates.rule: Provider changelog `.. note::` entries about minimum Airflow version requirements must not overstate the constraint when the provider still supports older Airflow versions via conditional feature activation
candidates.trigger: A `changelog.rst` note states a provider release *requires* Airflow X.Y when the provider actually still runs on older versions and only conditionally activates the new feature

candidates.rule: Airflow metrics documentation must refer to the stats system generically (supporting both statsd and OpenTelemetry), not solely as "statsd"
candidates.trigger: Documentation or comments describe Airflow's metrics/observability integration as "statsd" exclusively without mentioning OTel/OpenTelemetry

candidates.rule: SQL queries in Edge executor that filter on a newly-added DB column must guard against older schema versions where that column may not yet exist
candidates.trigger: A SQLAlchemy query in the Edge executor adds a `.where(Model.new_column == ...)` filter without a schema-version guard or migration check

candidates.rule: Tests for SQL safety/validation utilities must include a test case that exercises the exact call pattern used by the production operator (e.g. with `allowed_types=DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TYPES`)
candidates.trigger: New tests for a validation function omit the call signature used by the operator that owns it, leaving the operator's code path untested

candidates.rule: When a module is renamed or moved, the `common/compat/sdk.py` compatibility mapping must be updated to reflect the new module path
candidates.trigger: A module referenced in `providers/common/compat/src/airflow/providers/common/compat/sdk.py` is renamed but the mapping tuple still points to the old path

candidates.rule: Example values in `provider.yaml` configuration entries must be valid runtime values accepted by the underlying library, not file-extension aliases
candidates.trigger: A `provider.yaml` config entry has an `example:` value that is a file extension (e.g. `"gz"`) rather than the codec name the runtime code accepts (e.g. `"gzip"`)

candidates.rule: AI-toolset-specific API (retry exception mappings, AI retry hooks) must not be added to `DbApiHook`; keep such concerns in the AI toolset layer
candidates.trigger: A class attribute or method whose only consumer is `common/ai` is added to `DbApiHook` or another base hook shared by 10+ provider hooks

candidates.rule: Sync and deferred execution paths in an operator must emit equivalent log messages so task logs are comparable across both modes
candidates.trigger: A new sync code path in an operator that already has a deferred path omits progress log statements present in the deferred path (e.g. offset/page progress logging)

candidates.rule: In `.pyi` stubs, parameters whose runtime default is config-driven (`default_deferrable`, `default_pool`, etc.) must use `...` as the stub default, not a hardcoded literal
candidates.trigger: A `.pyi` stub declares `deferrable: bool = False` (or another hardcoded literal) for a parameter whose runtime default reads from Airflow configuration

candidates.rule: Optional provider dependencies must be guarded with a lazy import (try/except ImportError) rather than added as an unconditional entry in `pyproject.toml` dependencies
candidates.trigger: A new package is added to the `dependencies` list in a provider's `pyproject.toml` where the package is only used in one optional code path

candidates.rule: When fixing authentication-dispatch precedence in a hook, include a regression test asserting the new ordering when multiple auth extras are simultaneously set
candidates.trigger: A commit reorders if-branches in an `_get_token` or equivalent auth-dispatch method without adding a test for the case where both old and new conditions are truthy

candidates.rule: Set `team_name` on every Edge3 job row inserted into the database so the fetch endpoint can route jobs and callbacks correctly in multi-team setups
candidates.trigger: EdgeJobModel or equivalent job-row insert that omits a `team_name` field inside edge3 executor or callback-handling code

candidates.rule: Do not commit compiled UI `dist/` build artefacts for provider UIs; they must be built by Breeze or at provider-package build time and listed in `.gitignore`
candidates.trigger: Addition of `dist/` directory files (e.g. `main.d.ts`, `*.js`, `*.js.map`) under `providers/*/plugins/www/dist/`

candidates.rule: Do not describe `order_by` parameters as accepting comma-separated fields if the underlying `build_ordering()` helper only supports a single field
candidates.trigger: `order_by` query-parameter description containing "comma" or "separated by comma" in a route that calls `build_ordering()` with a single field

candidates.rule: Use `get_fab_auth_manager()` (or an `isinstance` check) instead of `cast(FabAuthManager, get_auth_manager())` to retrieve the FAB auth manager, and raise a clear exception when it is not configured
candidates.trigger: `cast("FabAuthManager", get_auth_manager())` or `cast(FabAuthManager, get_auth_manager())` in FAB provider route or helper code

candidates.rule: When dropping Edge3 ORM tables programmatically, pass `Model.__tablename__` (the string table name) rather than `Model.__table__` (the Table object) to the drop call
candidates.trigger: Reference to `EdgeWorkerModel.__table__`, `EdgeJobModel.__table__`, or `EdgeLogsModel.__table__` in a drop-table list or `Base.metadata.remove()` call

candidates.rule: Place Pydantic request/response datamodels for Edge3 worker UI routes in `datamodels_ui.py`, not inline in the route file
candidates.trigger: New Pydantic `BaseModel` class defined inside `providers/edge3/.../worker_api/routes/ui.py` instead of in `datamodels_ui.py`

candidates.rule: Use proper HTTP methods for Edge3 UI queue routes: `PUT /worker/{name}/queues` to replace the queue list, not `POST /worker/{name}/queues/add`
candidates.trigger: `@ui_router.post` decorator with an action-suffix path like `/queues/add` or `/queues/remove` in edge3 UI routes

candidates.rule: Add `testcontainers` as a shared dependency in `devel-common` rather than in individual provider `pyproject.toml` dev-dependency sections
candidates.trigger: `testcontainers` added to a `[project.optional-dependencies]` dev block in any provider's `pyproject.toml`

candidates.rule: Guard Airflow-2 log-upload code paths in providers with `if not AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS` rather than deleting them, so the provider continues to work against Airflow 2
candidates.trigger: Deletion of a log-upload or logging-handler code path in a provider that previously supported Airflow 2, without an `AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS` guard

candidates.rule: Use the existing `_build_es_search_response()` test helper to construct Elasticsearch response fixtures instead of hand-rolling response dicts
candidates.trigger: Hand-rolled ES response dict (e.g. `{"hits": {"total": ..., "hits": []}}`) used as a mock return value in elasticsearch provider tests

candidates.rule: Name FastAPI request/response datamodel classes `*Body` and `*Response`, not `*In` and `*Out`, to match the Airflow Core API naming convention
candidates.trigger: Pydantic model class name ending in `In` or `Out` (e.g. `RoleIn`, `RoleOut`) in any Airflow FastAPI datamodels file

candidates.rule: Import FastAPI utilities from `fastapi`, not directly from `starlette`, in provider route files
candidates.trigger: `from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException` or `from starlette import status` in a provider FastAPI route or dependency file

candidates.rule: Place FAB authorization helper functions (e.g. `requires_fab_custom_view`) in the service module, not in the route module, to mirror Airflow Core API conventions
candidates.trigger: Authorization dependency function defined inside a `routes/*.py` file rather than the corresponding `services/*.py` file in the FAB provider

candidates.rule: Use the AIRFLOW_V_X_Y_PLUS sentinel from version_compat instead of inline packaging.version.parse comparisons for Airflow version guards
candidates.trigger: packaging.version.parse(airflow_version) compared against a literal version string inside a provider

candidates.rule: Do not mutate Flask-AppBuilder's global Model.metadata at import time; scope metadata overrides to Airflow's own mapper registry only
candidates.trigger: Model.metadata = ... or assignment to Base.metadata at module level inside the FAB provider

candidates.rule: Operator execute_complete methods must branch explicitly on success, timeout, and error trigger statuses rather than collapsing all non-success states into a single error branch
candidates.trigger: execute_complete contains if event['status'] != 'success': raise ... without separate handling for timeout

candidates.rule: Every Google provider operator execute method must emit a self.log.info call describing the operation being performed
candidates.trigger: an operator execute() method in providers/google that calls a hook without a preceding or following self.log.info()

candidates.rule: Connection environment variable examples in provider docs must use URI format (not JSON object format) for AIRFLOW_CONN_* variables
candidates.trigger: provider .rst doc contains export AIRFLOW_CONN_<ID>='{...}' with a JSON object literal

candidates.rule: Provider pyproject.toml workaround dependencies must include a comment explaining the upstream issue and when the workaround can be removed
candidates.trigger: a transitive or pinned dependency added to pyproject.toml with only a brief inline comment but no upstream issue reference or removal condition

candidates.rule: When a new operator parameter will have its default value changed in a future release, accept None as the unset sentinel, default to None, and raise FutureWarning when None is detected rather than using the final default directly
candidates.trigger: a new operator __init__ parameter is added with a default value that a reviewer notes will change in a future release

candidates.rule: URL substring checks used for security-sensitive routing must validate that the trusted substring appears at the expected position (e.g. as the hostname), not anywhere in the URL string
candidates.trigger: if '<trusted-domain>' in url or similar substring check used to authenticate or route a request

candidates.rule: Prefer removing existing type: ignore suppressions rather than adding new suppression codes
candidates.trigger: diff adds a new mypy error code to an existing # type: ignore comment

candidates.rule: When running under Uvicorn (ASGI), remove the Flask/Werkzeug Date response header unconditionally so the server emits only one Date header
candidates.trigger: flask_app.after_request hook reads or conditionally removes the Date header when integrating with Uvicorn

candidates.rule: Derive the secure-cookie flag from both the request scheme and the ssl_cert config, not from ssl_cert alone
candidates.trigger: secure = bool(conf.get('api', 'ssl_cert', fallback='')) without checking request.base_url.scheme

candidates.rule: Use spec= or autospec= when creating Mock objects for SQLAlchemy sessions and ORM model instances in Airflow tests
candidates.trigger: Mock() or MagicMock() without spec= used for a session, role, or permission object in a provider test

candidates.rule: When a provider imports an API added in a recent version of another provider, guard the import with a try/except ImportError and early-return to maintain compatibility with older provider versions
candidates.trigger: unconditional import of a symbol from another provider's recently-added API module (e.g. airflow.providers.openlineage.api.*)

candidates.rule: In Google provider hooks, decompose compound resource-name strings (e.g. projects/{p}/locations/{l}/reasoningEngines/{id}) into individual parameters rather than accepting the full name as a single argument
candidates.trigger: a Google provider hook method accepts a parameter named `name` typed as str that represents a full GCP resource path

candidates.rule: Hook method parameter types must match the corresponding Google Cloud client library types exactly, not be widened to Any
candidates.trigger: a Google provider hook method uses Any for a parameter whose client counterpart has a concrete type (e.g. types.DeleteAgentEngineConfigOrDict)

candidates.rule: In Google provider hooks that use @GoogleBaseHook.fallback_to_default_project_id, describe project_id as optional in the docstring and position it last in the parameter list
candidates.trigger: a hook method decorated with @GoogleBaseHook.fallback_to_default_project_id documents project_id as 'Required' or places it before other parameters

candidates.rule: When a provider transfer operator exposes a passthrough config dict (e.g. `extra_config`), apply it last — after every top-level-derived field — so it actually wins for overlapping keys as documented
candidates.trigger: A passthrough dict is merged into an API-representation dict before the object is constructed, while top-level params (`schema_fields`, `max_bad_records`) are still assigned onto the constructed object afterwards

candidates.rule: Keep the `deferrable` constructor default as the inline literal `conf.getboolean("operators", "default_deferrable", fallback=False)`; do not switch it to `None` and resolve the config inside the body
candidates.trigger: An operator/sensor `__init__` signature changes `deferrable=conf.getboolean("operators", "default_deferrable", fallback=False)` to `deferrable=None` or any other default

candidates.rule: When bumping the documented `api_version` example of a marketing-platform/Google operator, update the versioned API documentation URLs in the same docstring to match
candidates.trigger: A docstring's `:param api_version:` example changes (e.g. 'v4' to 'v5') while a "Check official API docs" link in the same class docstring still contains the old `/rest/v4/` segment

candidates.rule: Collapse provider unit tests that differ only in one input and one expected value into a single test using `@pytest.mark.parametrize`
candidates.trigger: Two adjacent test functions such as `test_x_with_<flag>` / `test_x_without_<flag>` share an identical body apart from one argument and one assertion

candidates.rule: A test for an error-suppression flag (`ignore_error`, soft-fail behaviour) must make the mocked client raise the real provider exception via `side_effect` and assert nothing propagates — asserting that the flag was forwarded is not coverage
candidates.trigger: A new test exercising `ignore_error=True` only asserts `<method>.assert_called_once_with(..., on_error=mock.ANY)` and never sets `side_effect`

candidates.rule: Every public hook method added must get a unit test asserting the mocked client call chain arguments and the returned value, following the pattern already established in that test module
candidates.trigger: A hook gains public methods (e.g. `get_report`, `list_reports`) but the matching `providers/*/tests/unit/.../test_<hook>.py` only covers a subset of them

candidates.rule: Do not swallow credential-resolution or token-refresh failures inside a secrets backend; surface or chain the original error instead of letting it degrade into the backend's generic error
candidates.trigger: `except Exception: pass` (or an equally broad silent handler) wraps `credentials.refresh(...)` or a metadata-server lookup in a secrets backend or its internal client

candidates.rule: Resolve team-scoped secrets through the same `_get_team_or_global_secret` helper for connections, variables and config alike; do not gate it behind `conf.getboolean("core", "multi_team")`
candidates.trigger: A secrets backend getter branches on the `core.multi_team` config value to choose between the team-aware lookup and the plain lookup

candidates.rule: Tests for behaviour gated on an Airflow config flag must cover the flag-off state as well, using `conf_vars` to assert the legacy path is unchanged
candidates.trigger: Every new test wraps the call in `with conf_vars({("core", "multi_team"): "True"})` and no test exercises the same call with the flag disabled

candidates.rule: Async notifier and async execution paths must go through the provider's hook rather than opening a raw client session such as `aiohttp.ClientSession()` inline
candidates.trigger: An `async def async_notify`/async execute path constructs `aiohttp.ClientSession()` directly instead of awaiting the provider's async hook method

candidates.rule: `ui-field-behaviour` placeholders in `provider.yaml` must be valid literal JSON that a user can paste straight into a Connection `extra` field — never Python expressions or attribute references
candidates.trigger: A `placeholders.extra` block in `provider.yaml` contains a non-JSON token such as `cls.default_open_options` or any other Python expression

candidates.rule: Regenerate the provider metadata (`get_provider_info.py`) in the same change whenever `provider.yaml` is edited
candidates.trigger: A diff touches a `provider.yaml` (connection types, ui-field-behaviour, extras) with no matching update to that provider's generated `get_provider_info.py`

candidates.rule: Do not add a boolean opt-in flag for behaviour that only changes an operator's return value when existing users read the old value from a separate named XCom key
candidates.trigger: New `__init__` boolean parameter (e.g. `return_gcs_uris`) whose only effect is the format of the value returned by `execute()`, while the legacy value is still pushed to its own XCom key

candidates.rule: `get_conn()` must resolve connection-derived configuration into local variables and never overwrite attributes that were set in `__init__`
candidates.trigger: `get_conn()` assigns to `self.<param>` from `connection.extra_dejson` or a `getattr(..., default)` fallback chain

candidates.rule: Centralize an optional provider SDK import in a single helper that raises `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException`, instead of repeating a bare in-method `import` that surfaces a raw `ImportError`
candidates.trigger: The same third-party SDK (e.g. `import ibmmq`) is imported inside several methods of a hook/operator with no shared helper and no optional-feature exception

candidates.rule: Raise built-in exceptions such as `RuntimeError` for internal/programming errors in provider code instead of `AirflowException`
candidates.trigger: New `raise AirflowException(...)` added inside a provider package trigger, hook or operator helper for a state/invariant violation

candidates.rule: Log transient, retried API errors inside a trigger's async polling loop at info/debug level, or rate-limit them; do not emit a warning on every retry
candidates.trigger: `except <TransientError>` inside a trigger `run()` loop calls `self.log.warning(...)` immediately before `await asyncio.sleep(self.polling_period_seconds)`

candidates.rule: In a trigger, filter the result of a bulk list call that is already in scope rather than issuing one API request per item
candidates.trigger: A comprehension inside a trigger awaits `self.hook.get_<resource>(name=...)` once per name when a `list_<resources>()` result for the same namespace/label selector was already awaited

candidates.rule: When a trigger waits on state that only becomes true eventually (a pod reaching Succeeded, a job finishing), poll in a bounded `while` loop with a timeout instead of a single check plus a stale fallback
candidates.trigger: Trigger code performs one list/get call and then does `if not <resource>:` to fall back to a previously captured list rather than re-polling until the condition holds or a timeout expires

candidates.rule: Add new optional parameters to an existing provider hook or operator `__init__` as keyword-only arguments, placed after a `*` separator
candidates.trigger: A new optional parameter is inserted positionally into an existing `__init__` signature with no preceding `*` marker

candidates.rule: A provider hook/operator `:param:` docstring must describe the real runtime fallback and the real scope of validation — not the plausible-sounding one
candidates.trigger: A `:param X:` line claims a fallback such as "if None, the project ID from the connection is used" when the code passes `None` straight through, or a docstring summary claims to validate "format and existence" while only the format is checked

candidates.rule: Check that an optional credential capability is callable with `callable(getattr(credentials, "with_quota_project", None))` rather than probing it with `hasattr`
candidates.trigger: `if not hasattr(credentials, "<method>")` guards a subsequent call to that method on a google-auth credentials object

candidates.rule: Guard imports of optional cross-provider bases (e.g. BaseMessageQueueProvider) with a try/except that raises AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException when the dependency is absent
candidates.trigger: A provider module imports from another optional provider package (e.g. airflow.providers.common.messaging, airflow.providers.openlineage) at module top-level without a try/except AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException guard

candidates.rule: AssetWatcher triggers must use a while-True polling loop so the trigger never exits silently; a single await that can return None is not sufficient
candidates.trigger: A trigger's async run() method contains a single await call that can return None or raise, without an enclosing while True loop

candidates.rule: The OpenLineage JDBC authority extractor must strip userinfo (user:pass@) from the URL and handle Oracle thin URLs that use @// instead of ://
candidates.trigger: A _get_openlineage_authority or equivalent JDBC URL parser splits on :// without also handling @// (Oracle thin) and does not strip user:pass@ from the result

candidates.rule: Do not mutate sys.modules in a provider test package __init__.py; use a pytest fixture (monkeypatch.setitem) scoped to the relevant tests instead
candidates.trigger: sys.modules["..."] = ... appears in a tests/ package __init__.py rather than inside a pytest fixture or conftest

candidates.rule: Provider documentation examples targeting Airflow 3+ must use schedule= (not schedule_interval=) and import PythonOperator from airflow.providers.standard.operators.python
candidates.trigger: A provider README or docs example contains schedule_interval= or imports PythonOperator from airflow.operators.python when the provider's minimum Airflow version is 3

candidates.rule: Use wait_for_completion (not wait_for_termination) as the boolean parameter name for operators that poll until a job/resource finishes, for consistency with the AWS provider convention
candidates.trigger: An operator __init__ declares a parameter named wait_for_termination

candidates.rule: Guard imports of BaseEventTrigger / TriggerEvent with an AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS check and fall back to BaseTrigger for Airflow 2 compatibility
candidates.trigger: A provider trigger imports BaseEventTrigger or TriggerEvent from airflow.triggers.base unconditionally without an AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS guard

candidates.rule: An async (deferrable) hook must support the same connection extras as its synchronous counterpart; if an extra is unsupported, raise AirflowException explicitly rather than silently ignoring it
candidates.trigger: An async hook's credential-setup branch omits handling of connection extras (e.g. key_path, key_json) that the corresponding sync hook supports

candidates.rule: Tests for polling-retry loops must assert the sleep mock call count to verify the loop actually sleeps between polls
candidates.trigger: A test mocks time.sleep and tests a polling retry loop but does not assert mock_sleep.call_count

candidates.rule: In deferrable operators, do not use provisioning_state alone as a terminal-state signal for deferral decisions; only treat the container execution state as terminal
candidates.trigger: A deferrable operator checks cg_state.provisioning_state (e.g. 'Succeeded') as a condition to stop deferring, without also verifying instance_view.current_state

candidates.rule: When comparing cross-provider version strings use packaging.Version directly; do not wrap Version().base_version in another Version() call
candidates.trigger: Code contains Version(Version(...).base_version) when performing a cross-provider version comparison

candidates.rule: When an optional provider dependency is experimental or not yet default, place it in a named extras group rather than in the mandatory dependencies list
candidates.trigger: pyproject.toml of a provider adds a new dependency that is experimental, a protocol upgrade (e.g. psycopg3), or explicitly described as optional

candidates.rule: Only pass new connection kwargs in a Hook when the user has explicitly provided them, to avoid breaking existing behaviour
candidates.trigger: a Hook's get_conn() or connection-building method unconditionally passes a new keyword argument that previously had no default

candidates.rule: Use module-level try/except ImportError to detect optional library availability in providers; do not import optional libraries inside hook or operator methods at call time
candidates.trigger: a provider hook or operator method contains a bare `import` or `from … import` statement for an optional third-party library inside a function body

candidates.rule: When embedding client-identification metadata, use the full provider package name (e.g. apache-airflow-providers-redis) rather than 'apache-airflow', so the version reported matches the component being identified
candidates.trigger: provider code sets a client library name or driver_info string to 'apache-airflow' while using `provider_version`

candidates.rule: Use the NOTSET sentinel to distinguish 'user explicitly passed None' from 'parameter not provided' in Airflow 2.x compatibility code paths
candidates.trigger: code in an Airflow-2.x compat branch checks `getattr(self, attr) is not None` or `!= None` to decide whether a parameter was supplied by the user

candidates.rule: Do not set metadata["end_of_log"] = True when a log-fetch returns an empty result set; empty results may mean logs are not yet indexed, not that the task has finished logging
candidates.trigger: a task-log handler sets end_of_log to True inside an else/empty branch triggered by an empty logs_by_host or equivalent empty response

candidates.rule: When an optional SQLAlchemy or provider feature is unavailable at runtime, emit a warning rather than raising AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException, so the method can still return partial results from the SQL parser
